liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **My Brother Esau** (2 reviews): Wind and rain can be heard interfering with Bobby's singing on this tune [17][18]
- **Ramble On Rose** (2 reviews): Crew punched water out of a bulging tarp above Jerry's head before it burst [17][18]
- **Stella Blue** (1 review): A full moon rose over the clouds during this song [13]
- **Ship Of Fools** (1 review): Clouds broke during this song and a bright full moon appeared; the crowd cheered [15]
- **It's All Over Now, Baby Blue** (1 other source): Before this song, Bob joked about hail the size of beach balls, referring to that day's storms [7]

## Setlist highlights

- **gd84-06-13 s1 t01 Crowd Tuning**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [25]
- **gd84-06-13 s1 t02 Hell In A Bucket**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [25]
- **gd84-06-13 s1 t03 Candyman**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [25]
- **gd84-06-13 s1 t04 CC Rider**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [25]
- **gd84-06-13 s1 t05 Ramble On Rose**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [25]
- **gd84-06-13 s1 t06 My Brother Esau**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [25]
- **gd84-06-13 s1 t07 Cold Rain & Snow**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [25]
- **gd84-06-13 s1 t08 Don't Ease Me In**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [25]

## The recordings

- **gd1984-06-13.140183.fob.schoeps.cmc4.mk41.oade.bryant.miller.clugston.flac1644** (recommended): source not stated; 20 songs; 128 min [1]. Said about its sound: The Schoeps mk41 source sounds a little better than the Nakamichi 304 and Hecht AKG 330 versions, and is complete [22]
- **gd1984-06-13.164737.unknown.vita.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 19 songs; 134 min [5]
- **gd1984-06-13.148194.beyerm88.holbrook.flac2448**: source not stated; 19 songs; 134 min [7]. Said about its sound: Beyerdynamic M88 recording has slight dropouts from 3:13 through 3:32 in one track [7]
- **gd1984-06-13.148390.2nd.set.akg.d330bt.senn421.hecht.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 13 songs; 90 min [11]

## Around the show

- Thunder, lightning and huge hail battered Denver in the distance while Red Rocks was spared the storm [13]
- Listener snuck in hidden in a car trunk while selling stickers, then saw Jerry step out of a limo and greet him [14]
- An overhead tarp collected gallons of rain and emptied onto Bobby, drenching him [15]
- Bob mentioned hail; actually Arvada, five miles away, took the heavy damage, though it hailed briefly at the Rocks [16]
- Wind gusts kept dumping water from the stage tarp, and Bobby got drenched [16]
- This night had the most rain of the run; tarp water emptied onto Bobby, risky given the amplification [21]
- A hailstorm in the city did major damage; Boulder's Events Center was readied on standby but not used [21]
- Bob asked how many would come if they played in the morning; the crowd roared after the drenching afternoon [7]
- The run improved slightly each night, each with different highlights [21]
- Reviewer prefers this source to the Hecht upload, which is incomplete, and to the Suraci Nakamichi 304 [22]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1984-06-13.140183.fob.schoeps.cmc4.mk41.oade.bryant.miller.clugston.flac1644**: taped by Robert Bryant patched out of Oade Brothers; transferred by Charlie Miller and Scott Clugston; source: (FOB) Schoeps CMC4/MK41 > Oade M118 > Cassette Master (Sony WM-D6C/Denon DXM-90) [1]. Also: The Nakamichi 304 source (shnid 78363) supplies a 35-second patch in Hell In A Bucket plus banter and tuning [1]
- **gd1984-06-13.164737.unknown.vita.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Jim Vita; transferred by Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Master Audience Cassettes; Unknown Equipment > Jim Vita's 1st Generation Cassette [5]. Also: First-generation cassettes from Jim Vita, transferred by Charlie Miller; Hecht's Neumann KM84i source patches 46 seconds in Drums [5]
- **gd1984-06-13.148194.beyerm88.holbrook.flac2448**: taped by Executive Crew - Tom Pinney, Kyle Holbrook, Sean Murtha, Chris Kidwell; transferred by Kyle Holbrook; source: MAUD CA: Beyer M88's XY > Sony TCD5M|maxell MX90 x2 no NR ***[Hell in A Bucket from first generation same source] Location: 80 feet from stage DFC 7 feet up [7]
- **gd1984-06-13.148390.2nd.set.akg.d330bt.senn421.hecht.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Chris Hecht; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: Chris Hecht's Master Audience Cassettes; (2) AKG D330BT mics + (1) Sennheiser 421 > Fostex Mixer > Sony D5M [11]. Also: Nakamichi 304 source supplies Bob's intro and first China Cat notes, plus a 42-second patch in Drums [11]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Steven Rood Grateful Dead: [1984-06-14 Red Rocks Amphitheatre, Morrison, CO, USA - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/show/1984-06-14-red-rocks-amphitheatre-morrison-co-usa/) [26]
- Poster by Steve Schneider Grateful Dead: [1984-06-13 Red Rocks Amphitheatre, Morrison, CO, USA - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/show/1984-06-13-red-rocks-amphitheatre-morrison-co-usa/) [27]

Wind gusts kept dumping water from the stage tarp, and Bobby got drenched
Wind and rain can be heard interfering with Bobby's singing on this tune

The run improved slightly each night, each with different highlights
